\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{طلاق} (talâq)}{طلاق (talâq)}]{\fa{طلاق} (talâq) — a divorce}

\label{lesson:FA-C336-talaq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a mahr, then the Persian for a trousseau.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{طلاق}}
\textbf{\fa{طلاق}} (\emph{talâq}) — \textquotedblleft{}a divorce\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{طلاق} \fa{آنها} \fa{برای} \fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{سخت} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Talâq-e ânhâ barâ-ye bachche-hâ sakht bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Their divorce was hard on the children.
\end{quote}

Traditionally \emph{talâq dâdan} is said of the husband.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{talâq} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṭalāq}, \textquotedblleft{}divorce\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{talâq}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{talâq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{talâq}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a mahr, then the Persian for a trousseau, then say \emph{talâq} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{طلاق} \fa{گرفتن} (talâq gereftan)}{طلاق گرفتن (talâq gereftan)}]{\fa{طلاق} \fa{گرفتن} (talâq gereftan) — to get divorced}

\label{lesson:FA-C336-talaq-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a trousseau, then the Persian for a divorce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{طلاق} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{طلاق} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{talâq gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to get divorced\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آنها} \fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{ده} \fa{سال} \fa{طلاق} \fa{گرفتند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ânhâ ba'd az dah sâl talâq gereftand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They got divorced after ten years.
\end{quote}

With \emph{az}: \emph{az shoharash talâq gereft} \textquotedblleft{}she divorced her husband\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{talâq migirad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{talâq} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṭalāq} (EtymDB); \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian, from the Old Persian root \emph{grab-} \textquotedblleft{}to seize\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{talâq gereftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{talâq gereftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a trousseau, then the Persian for a divorce, then say \emph{talâq gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بیوه} (bive)}{بیوه (bive)}]{\fa{بیوه} (bive) — a widow; widowed}

\label{lesson:FA-C336-bive}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a divorce, then the Persian for to get divorced.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بیوه}}
\textbf{\fa{بیوه}} (\emph{bive}) — \textquotedblleft{}a widow; widowed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادربزرگم} \fa{سی} \fa{سال} \fa{بیوه} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâdarbozorgam si sâl bive bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandmother was a widow for thirty years.
\end{quote}

Mostly of women; \emph{mard-e bive} is \textquotedblleft{}a widower\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bive} is a native Persian word. EtymDB lists it without a parent, so its deeper origin is not settled here.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a divorce, then the Persian for to get divorced, then say \emph{bive} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{یتیم} (yatim)}{یتیم (yatim)}]{\fa{یتیم} (yatim) — an orphan}

\label{lesson:FA-C336-yatim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to get divorced, then the Persian for a widow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{یتیم}}
\textbf{\fa{یتیم}} (\emph{yatim}) — \textquotedblleft{}an orphan\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{از} \fa{کودکی} \fa{یتیم} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U az kudaki yatim bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He had been an orphan since childhood.
\end{quote}

Broken plural \emph{aytâm}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yatim} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{yatīm}, \textquotedblleft{}orphan\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرپرستی} (sarparasti)}{سرپرستی (sarparasti)}]{\fa{سرپرستی} (sarparasti) — custody, guardianship}

\label{lesson:FA-C336-sarparasti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a widow, then the Persian for an orphan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرپرستی}}
\textbf{\fa{سرپرستی}} (\emph{sarparasti}) — \textquotedblleft{}custody, guardianship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سرپرستی} \fa{بچه} \fa{با} \fa{مادرش} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sarparasti-ye bachche bâ mâdarash ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child's mother has custody.
\end{quote}

\emph{sar} \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{} + \emph{parast} \textquotedblleft{}one who tends\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-i}. Also \textquotedblleft{}supervision\textquotedblright{} at work.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sarparasti} is built from Persian \emph{sar} \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{} and \emph{parast-}, the stem of \emph{parastidan} \textquotedblleft{}to tend, to worship\textquotedblright{}, with the noun suffix \emph{-i}. All of it is native.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sarparasti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sarparasti}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a widow, then the Persian for an orphan, then say \emph{sarparasti} again
